steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Finance cannot reconcile instance uptime. A metered machine in an account dedicated to one customer belongs to that customer regardless of which customer its tags name, including when they name none. A shared-account machine may belong to several customers and its uptime must be divided evenly among tenants genuinely onboarded for that account; unknown or unplaceable usage stays off the bill. The onboarding records in the metering bucket beside the account list identify billable customers. Update the metering sweep so published uptime follows those rules. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials

-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)

-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))

steps.message:
Changes complete:

- **`src/utils/aws/s3.ts`**: added `listKeys` (paginated `ListObjectsV2`) and `getDocumentsUnderPrefix` so collectors can read every per-customer onboarding record sitting beside the account list.
- **`src/onboarding/entities/meteringAccounts.entity.ts`**: added `OnboardedAccount` / `CustomerOnboardingRecord` (with the `dedicated` flag), `parseTaggedCustomerIds`, and `OnboardedCustomers`, an account-indexed view of the onboarding records that answers "who owns this machine?": dedicated account → its single customer regardless of tags (even untagged), shared account → the tagged customers genuinely onboarded for that account, anything else → nobody (empty list). An account claimed as dedicated by two customers is treated as shared. `MeteringRegistry` gained `customerPrefix` (falls back to `customers/` beside the registry key) and `loadOnboardedCustomers`.
- **`src/microservices/ec2InstanceDataGatherer/ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.ts`**: the sweep now loads onboarding records, resolves owners per instance, splits the running-time increment evenly among co-tenants, logs and drops unplaceable usage, and rounds away float dust.
- Added unit tests (`ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.spec.ts`) covering dedicated accounts, even splitting, non-onboarded tag values, unplaceable usage, conflicting dedication claims, and dimension filtering. Verified against the emulator: `cus_harbor 0.291666655` (3 dedicated instances + half of the shared one), `cus_lattice 0.124999995` (half shared + one full), untagged shared instance off the bill.
